overview.alt: Auto settings and the Buddha source model
overview.caption: Auto settings and the Buddha source model. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Set the model type, topology and target count.
Choose the texture resolution and output format.
Run the complete workflow with Rebuild Asset.

installation.alt: Rebuilt installed as a Blender extension
installation.caption: Rebuilt installed as a Blender extension. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Get Extensions is the extension installation and management section.
Rebuilt appears under Installed after installation.
Open this menu to use Install from Disk.

preferences.caption: Rebuilt addon preferences. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Set 0 for Automatic, or enter a custom memory limit in GiB.
Open Installation Folder locates the installed extension.

manual.caption: The four Manual workflow stages. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Switch to Manual.
Open a stage to adjust its settings; use the arrow on the right to run it.
Review the asset summary and progress.

retopology.alt: Retopology settings and low mesh wireframe
retopology.caption: Retopology settings and low mesh wireframe. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Set the target count and choose Strict or Dynamic.
Tune detail preservation for the model.
Review the actual result: this example produced 8,362 quads.

seams.alt: Generated seam cuts on the Buddha
seams.caption: Generated seam cuts on the Buddha. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Choose Balanced or Fewer islands and whether to preserve marked seams.
Recalculate the generated seams.
Accept your manually edited seams with Use Existing Seams.

unwrap.caption: The packed UV layout. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Choose the unwrap method, packer, search time, rotation and padding.
Open the UV review with Show UVs.
Inspect the packed islands inside a single UV tile.

existing.alt: Controls for accepting an existing UV layout
existing.caption: Controls for accepting an existing UV layout. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Use Existing UVs accepts the current layout without unwrapping or repacking it.

bake.alt: Bake Maps and texture output settings
bake.caption: Bake Maps and texture output settings. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Select the maps to transfer from the source.
Choose the resolution and normal space.
Set the texture file format and bit depth.

export.caption: Export destination and format. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Choose Unity, Unreal or Godot.
Export the selected completed asset.

unity.alt: Unity export and render pipeline selection
unity.caption: Unity export and render pipeline selection. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Choose Unity.
The format is displayed as a read-only label.
Match the render pipeline to your Unity project.

unreal.alt: Unreal export as a self-contained GLB
unreal.caption: Unreal export as a self-contained GLB. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Choose Unreal.
glTF (.glb) is the fixed format for this destination.
Write a self-contained GLB into the asset folder.

godot.alt: Godot export as a self-contained GLB
godot.caption: Godot export as a self-contained GLB. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Choose Godot.
glTF (.glb) is the fixed format for this destination.
Write a self-contained GLB into the asset folder.

report.caption: Completed asset and quality reports. Click to enlarge.

marks.label: Compare the achieved count with the requested target.
Read the shape and topology checks.
Review any warnings before deciding whether to continue or change settings.
